_comment: Mutations that reintroduce the ORIGINAL emergency-stop defect, one at a time.
All seven were observed KILLED on 2026-10-16 except E, which survives by
design: the test monkeypatches EMERGENCY_STOP_PERSIST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS so the
suite stays fast, which means it defends the timeout WRAPPER (see G) and not
the production VALUE. That is a deliberate trade, recorded here so a future
reader does not 'fix' E into the list expecting it to fail.
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

mutations.label: A: no persistence at all (the original defect)
mutations.replace:
return  # MUTANT: never persisted
        if not self.redis_client:
            logger.critical(
                "[EmergencyStop] Engaged but there is no redis_client; the latch "

mutations.label: B: clear does not erase the Redis key
C: restore fails OPEN when Redis is unreadable
D: restore reads the key but ignores it
mutations.replace: return  # MUTANT: read the key, ignored it

mutations.label: E: production timeout VALUE raised (survives by design -- see G)
mutations.expected_survivor_reason: The suite monkeypatches EMERGENCY_STOP_PERSIST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS so the tests stay fast, so it defends the timeout WRAPPER (mutation G) and deliberately does not pin the production VALUE.

mutations.label: F: API key drifts from the key the bot reads
G: timeout wrapper waits forever (this is what defends the kill switch)
